transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess I just keep getting these flashes. They kind of hit me out of nowhere. Like, I could just be standing at a pickup counter for work, and... suddenly it's like I'm right back in that crowded holding room. Just... seeing the fight happen all over again. Hearing everybody getting shoved up against the wall. It just... keeps hitting me. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
What happens right before these flashes occur?
I'm not really sure. Um... nothing, I guess. Like I said, it just kind of... happens. I haven't noticed anything specific.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or situations because of these flashes?

Yeah... I guess so. I've been, um, taking the long way around town on my routes. Turning down the night runs. I just... I can't really make myself go anywhere near that detention building right now. 

And I don't really want to talk about what happened, either. If I do, it just... it feels like I'm right back there. So I just try to avoid it.
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?

Yeah, sleep's... it's not really happening. I might doze off for an hour, maybe two. Then I just wake up. Usually from some dream about being in that cell, or just hearing a door slam. And then I can't go back to sleep. By the time morning comes around, I'm just... too wrecked to even think about driving my route.
Do you find yourself jumping or getting startled easily by loud noises or unexpected movements?

Yeah. I mean... yeah. It's bad. Um... if my radio crackles, or... or I hear a siren... even just someone shutting a door too hard. I just... I jump. Like I'm bracing for someone to rush me. And then my heart just goes crazy. It beats so hard I... I usually have to pull the van over, or just step outside if I'm on foot. Just to catch my breath.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened in that holding room?
No. Not really. I mean... I was just making a delivery. I didn't do anything wrong. I was just... in the wrong place. So, no. I don't feel like it was my fault.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when these flashes happen?
No. I don't... I don't really know what you mean by that. When it happens, I just feel like I'm back in that room. I'm not watching from the outside. I'm just... there.
Do you have difficulty concentrating or focusing on things?
Not really. I mean... I drive all day. You kind of just do it. It's automatic. So... no. I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you find yourself always being on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in a safe environment?
No. I don't think so. I mean... I just do my route and go home. I'm not really looking around for... threats or anything. So, no.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from yourself or the world around you?
No. I don't... I wouldn't say that. I just do my routine. I don't feel numb or anything.
Do you often find yourself scanning your surroundings, even when you're in a place that feels safe?
I... didn't you just ask me that? Like I said, no. I'm not really looking over my shoulder or anything. I just do my job.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened in the holding room?

I... yeah. I guess. I mean, I don't really want to talk about it. If I do, it just... it feels like I'm right back there. 

So I just try not to. I've been turning down my night runs... taking the long way around town. I just can't make myself go anywhere near that detention building.
How long have you been experiencing these flashes and sleep disturbances?
About a week, I guess. Just... ever since they detained me overnight. Since I saw that... the assault in the holding area.
Have you avoided any social activities or relationships because of these flashes or to avoid reminders of what happened?

Yeah. I guess. I... I stopped going to my volunteer things. I just can't really keep it together around a bunch of people right now. 

And... I don't know, it's messing up work, too. I've already missed two shifts. When I do try to go out and do my deliveries, I just... I don't feel safe driving. I'm just too shaken up and on edge.
Have you avoided any other activities or places besides the detention building and night runs because of these flashes?
No... not really. Just the stuff I already mentioned. I mostly just stay home right now anyway.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like tremors, headaches, or stomach problems when these flashes happen?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed my stomach or anything like that. Just... what I already told you.
Have you stopped doing anything else you normally enjoy because of these flashes or to avoid thinking about what happened?
No, I... I don't think so. Like I said, I'm just mostly staying home. There's not really much else I do anyway.
How often do these flashes happen to you in a typical day?
I don't really know. I don't... I don't count them or anything. They just happen. I'm not sure.
